actor: User A is a synthetic authenticated trade-reader. User B is a separate synthetic account. No production data is used.
workspaces: W-A and W-B are workspace IDs, not browser tabs. W-A contains trade X. W-B contains positions Y. Authorized fixture data establishes access to both.
browser_tabs: B-A and B-B are separate browser tabs. Test setup records whether they share one origin and profile.
service: A protected fixture endpoint accepts only its configured synthetic current credential and returns principal, request ID, and operation ID.
renewal: A successful renewal means the response supplies usable current access and the protected fixture accepts that access. Dialog closure alone is insufficient.
time: tE is the issued access expiry. tR is issued refresh expiry. Time is controlled unless a real-clock run is declared. Fixture durations are not production policy.
loading: Global loading is the shell isLoading state. Workspace loading includes its lazy module, data request, or grid state. They are measured separately.
ui: Use source-derived controls from workspace-transport-components.json. Verify exact target identity and runtime uniqueness before binding browser actions.
transport: Synthetic GraphQL and STOMP peers record handshake identity, connection ID, topic, message ID, acknowledgements, and closure. Never record raw credentials.
isolation: Use an isolated origin, synthetic accounts, unique operation IDs, and explicit pre/post storage snapshots. Do not run mutation cases against production.
cleanup: Close all test tabs and sockets, abort held requests, remove synthetic records, clear isolated storage, and restore clock/network controls after every case.
execution: All definitions are NOT_RUN. Parent catalog owns canonical Gherkin. These records are design inputs, not a parallel published specification.
basis: target means cited target requirement; observed means source-derived current design; proposed-security needs security-owner review; policy-open cannot receive acceptance.
